detailed_rationale:
Happiest Minds Technologies is a digital-first IT services company (Product & Digital Engineering Services is 79% of revenue) serving BFSI, EdTech, Healthcare, Industrial & Manufacturing, Hi-Tech & Media and Retail & Logistics clients. FY26 revenue grew to Rs 2,315 Cr from Rs 2,061 Cr (+12.3%), with profit up to Rs 213 Cr from Rs 185 Cr (+15%), and momentum has if anything accelerated into FY27 -- Q1 FY27 revenue grew 14.3% year-on-year. This is a genuinely healthy growth rate relative to most of the Indian mid-cap IT services peer set at present, most of whom are grappling with flat-to-low-single-digit growth.

The item we want to flag clearly is debt: borrowings rose from Rs 512 Cr (FY24) to Rs 1,494 Cr (FY26), roughly a threefold increase -- unusual for what is typically an asset-light IT services model. We could not determine from the sources available whether this is core financial borrowing or substantially lease-liability recognition (common under Ind AS 116 for IT companies with large owned/leased campuses), so we flag this as a genuine open question rather than asserting either explanation. Promoter holding has declined steadily (53.25% in Mar 2021 to 44.21% by Jun 2026), which screener itself flags as a watch item, though this level of gradual founder-holding dilution is not unusual for a founder-led IT company diversifying over time.

Return ratios are decent but not exceptional for an asset-light IT model (ROE 13.8%, ROCE 13.3%) -- lower than the company's own historical high-growth-era returns (Happiest Minds posted ROE well above 20% in 2021-2022), suggesting some moderation in capital efficiency even as growth has stayed healthy.
recommendation_rationale: Hold, matching the quant score -- genuinely strong and accelerating revenue growth (a rarity in the current mid-cap IT environment) supports at least a Hold, but the unexplained near-tripling of debt and moderated return ratios versus the company's own history keep us from describing this as more than a Hold until the debt composition is better understood.
summary: Happiest Minds Technologies, a digital engineering and IT services company, delivered healthy and accelerating revenue growth through FY26 and into the June 2026 quarter (14.3% year-on-year), well above the industry average at present. Borrowings have risen substantially over the past two years, and we could not confirm from available data how much of that reflects real financial debt versus accounting for office leases. We rate it a Hold: strong growth momentum, but a debt trend worth understanding better before extending more confidence.
positive_para: Revenue growth has been genuinely strong and accelerating (FY26 +12.3%, Q1 FY27 +14.3% year-on-year) at a time when most mid-cap Indian IT peers are struggling for growth at all, profit has grown in line, and the company maintains a healthy dividend payout (42-49%) alongside that growth.
negative_para: Borrowings have nearly tripled over two years (Rs 512 Cr to Rs 1,494 Cr), and we could not verify from the sources available how much of this is core financial debt versus lease-liability accounting -- a genuine data gap rather than a confirmed problem, but one we flag honestly. Return ratios (ROE 13.8%, ROCE 13.3%) are also moderate relative to the company's own stronger historical return profile, and promoter holding has declined steadily over five years.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At roughly 27x earnings against mid-teens revenue growth, the valuation is reasonable if the current growth acceleration holds and the debt increase proves to be largely a lease-accounting effect rather than genuine leverage; it would look less comfortable if the debt is real balance-sheet borrowing being used to fund working capital or capacity in a business that has historically been asset-light. We would want the debt composition clarified before getting more constructive than Hold.
